newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan firms ponder visits to Iraq for oil talks.
newsitem.headline: Japan firms ponder visits to Iraq for oil talks.

text.p: Japanese traders expressed an interest on Tuesday in meeting Iraqi officials to discuss a possible deal to buy crude oil, and at least one trading company has already dispatched an employee to Baghdad.

Last month Iraq accepted U.N. terms to allow it to make a limited shipment of crude oil to global markets for the first time since an export ban was imposed on the country for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Tokyo traders said that while they did not expect a Japanese firm to be among the first to sign an oil deal with Iraq, there was interest in possible future purchases.
One trader with a leading trading house which has occasionally sent officials to Baghdad in the past six years said one was now on his way to the Iraqi capital.
The company was unlikely to reach an agreement on this visit, but the official was being sent "with a mind to doing more serious business" this time, the trader said.
Other traders with trading firms and oil companies said they had not yet decided to send officials, but were likely to do so in the future.
Iraq's state oil firm SOMO has asked potential buyers to give dates for meetings in Baghdad to negotiate contract terms.
